hypotheses.basis: The policy uses 'only' to impose a cardinality restriction on tool calls per turn. 'One tool call at a time' means at most one tool call may be issued in a single turn; exceeding this violates the rule.
unresolved_terms: at a time (could mean per-turn or per-action-step; mapped to per-turn given available atoms)

hypotheses.basis: The word 'should' (rather than 'must') may indicate a soft recommendation rather than a hard prohibition. Under this reading, issuing more than one tool call per turn is discouraged but not strictly forbidden — the agent may violate it when justified, changing the obligation from a prohibition to a preference. The cardinality atom still applies but the consequence of violation is weaker.
unresolved_terms: what constitutes sufficient justification to override a soft recommendation

hypotheses.basis: 'At a time' may refer to temporal concurrency (only one tool call active/in-flight at any moment) rather than turn-level issuance cardinality. Under this reading, an agent may issue multiple tool calls in a single turn as long as they execute sequentially (one completes before the next begins). The prohibition is against parallel/concurrent execution, not against multiple calls per turn. This is behaviorally distinct: batching sequential calls in one turn would be permitted.

whether sequential issuance within a turn counts as 'one at a time'
